NOT purely patient-identity-only (a real [-3,+45]-day temporal window is applied, and a used[] flag prevents any lab row being assigned to more than one episode) -- so this does NOT meet the audit brief's strict definition of HIGH RISK ('associated only by canonical patient identity without episode-level temporal attribution'). However, the greedy assignment processes episodes in ascending consult_date order and gives each the nearest unused lab record in its window; for a patient with two teleconsultations close together, the earlier episode can claim a lab record that temporally belongs to the later one. This mis-assignment mode is not quantified anywhere in the pipeline output. Classified IMPLEMENTED WITH KNOWN ISSUE, not HIGH RISK, but the exact mis-assignment rate is unmeasured.
